lines.note: Continues the preceding fish-scaling sense of fuqu. Qeuo toru is a regional alternative; qe must not be interpreted solely from the modern ordinary meaning 'hair'.
Completes Alicubi, 'in some places', followed by Idem. This is Latin explanatory material, not Japanese or a new headword.
Fuqi here is roofing: iye or yaneuo fuqu, to roof a house. The abbreviated u principal part is retained rather than editorially expanded to qu.
Telhar, ou cobrir a caſa confirms the roofing sense, distinct from the blowing entry below. The entire short line fits its crop.
Fuqi now means blowing or wind. Vſo continues below as an example of whistling, not the familiar modern ordinary sense 'lie'.
Vſouo fuqu is whistling, Aſuuiar. Caiuo fuqu then introduces blowing a shell; cai is historical kai.
The shell is explained by buzina or buzio, a horn or conch. Fiuo fuqu begins the fire example, not a continuation of the conch's name.
Fiuo fuqu means blow on a fire, whereas Cajega fuqu means wind blows. Semantics distinguishes f from long ſ without deciding typographic s length.
Fuqiacaxi is fuki-akashi, blowing or playing through the night. The generated kana's potential qi+a contraction must not obscure this compound boundary.
Yofitoi and divided yomoſugara are all-night expressions. Frauta is the printed historical Portuguese spelling and is not modernized.
Completes yomoſugara fuyeuo fuqiacaita: played the flute all night. The -aita conjugation is historical, not an error to replace with modern -ashita.
Completes frauta toda a noite. The short continuation is a real physical line, not blank space to remove.
Fuqiague is fuki-age, wind lifting something. The aguru principal part and examples clarify the compound despite a contracted automatic kana hint.
Sudareuo fuqiaguru concerns the wind raising a blind. The Portuguese algũa is divided between physical lines.

runs.text: Aleuantar o vẽto as eſteiras da porta. ¶

lines.note: The gloss specifies the door's mats or blinds. Final Na begins Namiuo below, not an independent Japanese word.
Completes Namiuo fuqiaguru: wind raises waves. No hyphen is supplied after on merely because ondas divides here.
Completes ondas muito alto and introduces Fuyeuo fuqiaguru. The flute example gives aguru a finishing rather than spatially upward sense.

runs.text: Acabar de tanger com a frauta, ou dar ſinal

lines.note: Playing the flute is finished, or a signal of ending given. This sense follows the Japanese example rather than the wave example.
Completes de acabar, 'of finishing'. It is the remainder of the flute gloss, not another entry.
Fuqiaraxi is fuki-arashi, blowing violently. The divided Caje gives wind as the subject of the following example.
Completes Cajega fuqi araſu. The visible space within the compound is retained rather than silently normalized.
Fuqiare is referred to the same violent-wind sense by Idem. Its inflection is distinct from the preceding araſu formation.
Fuqiberi is the loss of silver during smelting, not ordinary wind. The scan ends fundição with o, correcting OCR c.
Fuqicacari concerns wind or fire striking something. The abbreviated u principal part is preserved as printed.
Miǒqua tôzai yori introduces a conflagration from east and west. The Portuguese below instead says east and south; preserve that source-level discrepancy.
Completes fuqicacatte and cites Taif., Lib. 15. Taif. is Roman, the bibliographical portion italic, with the full stop kept with its Roman label.

runs.text: o incendio aleuantado do Leste, & Sul.

lines.note: The scan reads Leste, & Sul. It does not literally agree with Japanese tôzai, but neither passage should be rewritten to harmonize the dictionary.
Fuqicaqe is fuki-kake, blowing onto something. Ventoſobre is close-set in print; modern word separation alone is not grounds to alter it.
The gloss extends to raising a fire. The example below illustrates that sense rather than beginning another headword.
Cajega miǒquauo fuqicaqete describes wind raising a great blaze. The second long-o mark is weak; retain the baseline rather than resolve its exact shape from meaning.

runs.text: tando o vento grande labareda, & incendio.

lines.note: Completes Aleuantando and the large flame or conflagration. This confirms the fiery sense of miǒqua.
Fuqicaraxi is fuki-karashi, withering by wind. It must not be confused with the earlier fuki-arashi entry.
Cuſa, qiuo fuqicaraſu has grass and trees as objects. Se continues as Secar below; no unprinted hyphen is added.

runs.text: car o vento as eruas, & aruores.

lines.note: Completes wind drying herbs and trees. The plural Portuguese matches the collective Japanese objects.
Fuqicayexi means overturn by wind. The enlarged weakened initial of eita, together with NINJAL's recorded principal part, supports eita rather than OCR cita; do not normalize it to aita.
Completes algũa couſa. The short line is genuine, with the whole word and its period visible.
Fuqicudaqi means break by wind. The italic initial is Q in Quebrar, correcting OCR O; qu is the Japanese principal part.
Taifùga cozuyeuo fuqicudai- describes a great wind breaking treetops. The worn accent on Taifù is retained as a qualified reading, not standardized from expected pronunciation.
Naguiſani iſagouo tobaſuru describes sand thrown on the shore. The damaged g has residual scan support, reinforced by Portuguese areas; OCR y obscured the word.

runs.text: do o vẽto os raminhos de cima dos cumes das

lines.note: The Portuguese describes branches at the treetops broken by wind. The crop contains the descending strokes despite the sloping baseline.

runs.text: aruores, & fazendo ſaltar as areas da praya.

lines.note: Completes the trees and beach-sand description. The scan supports fazendo rather than OCR fuzendo; praya remains historical spelling.
Fuqicudaxi is explained by Fuqiuoroſu, blowing downward. The explanatory i, is not part of the Japanese reading.
Completes de cima pera baixo, from above downward. Pera is retained rather than changed to modern para.
Fuqicuzzuxi means destruction by wind. Change OCR capital I to visible long ſ in ſu; retain unusual uita, supported by scan and headword data, rather than normalizing to aita.
Completes algua couſa. Faint printing does not justify automatically adding a nasal mark.
Fuqide concerns a rash beginning to appear. The worn second letter is u with scan and lexical support, correcting OCR Faqide.
The damaged formula is read ou couſa ſemelhante from surviving strokes and syntax. Caſaga fuqiz- begins the example; the scan's continuation stroke is not a sentence period.
Completes fuqizzuru, the rash breaking out. This bottom continuation is body text rather than a catchword.
Fuqifanachi is fuki-hanachi, wind detaching or separating something. The f represents historical h; the Portuguese continuation needs no invented hyphen.
Completes separar o vento algũa couſa. Wind is the agent, not the object being separated.
Fuqifarai is fuki-harai, wind sweeping away. Retain the open long-o principal parts visible in the scan.
Completes the alternative 'carry everything away'. The short line and final period are fully visible.
Fǔqifucutacu means wealth and prosperity. The damaged initial F, independently corroborated by NINJAL, corrects the OCR's B.

runs.text: Vento que ſopra em contrario do

lines.note: Fuqigayexi names a contrary wind. The voiced g is not forced to the unvoiced spelling found in neighboring verbs.
Completes outro, the opposing wind. This tiny continuation is body text, not furniture.
The second Fuqigayexi names the helmet's turned-back flaps. Abas do capacete distinguishes this material object from wind.
Fuqiidaxi has two i letters visible in the scan and recorded by NINJAL. It is blowing something out; the extra i must not disappear.
Adds Desbrochar, bursting forth, qualified by force below. Modern associations with budding should not narrow the dictionary's meaning.
Com rijo não podendo terſe describes an uncontrollable forceful outburst. Retain the old phrasing rather than recast it.
Fuqijde is fuki-ide, beginning to blow. The j marks the second i, not modern Japanese ji.

runs.text: ¶ Item, Começar a ſair ſarna. Vt,

lines.note: The entry also applies to a rash emerging. Caſa- is the Japanese rash term, not Portuguese caſa 'house'.
Completes Caſaga fuqi izzuru. Preserve the visible spacing and historical izzuru spelling.
Fuqimacuri describes wind lifting a roof. Utta is visible and recorded by NINJAL; it is not automatically replaced by expected atta.

runs.text: o vento as telhas do telhado. Vt,

lines.note: The gloss specifies roof tiles, and Yaneuo begins the example with the roof as object.
Fuqi macuru is glossed as unroofing the roof. The internal printed space remains, and the sense is physical rather than figurative.
Fuqimidaxi means wind throwing into disorder. Emburilhar is retained as printed instead of modernized.

runs.text: uoluer o vento algũa couſa. Vt,

lines.note: The definition continues with turning things. Fuqimi- begins the participial example below.
Fuqimidaxitaru fonouo is a flame buffeted by wind. Fonouo means flame; retain its historical spelling.
Completes the wind's turning and tossing the flame. Both Portuguese verbs describe the same example.
Fuqimodoxi means blowing back, here turning a vessel back. Enlarged print and NINJAL both support oita despite expected aita, so retain it with this qualification.
The object is embarcação, a vessel. This clarifies the nautical sense of arribar.
Fuqimucai describes a contrary wind. Both open long-o marks in the principal parts remain legible.
Fuqin and fuiqin are referred to preferred Foiqin, a wiping cloth. Melius is Latin editorial wording, not Japanese.
The cloth cleans goquis and tables. The italic Japanese bowl term goquis is one word in the scan, correcting the OCR's internal space.
Fuqinabiqe means bending plants through wind. The principal parts identify a transitive formation.
Plants and herbs complete the objects being bent. The entire short gloss remains in the crop.
Fuqinagaxi is a tubular streamer or windsock. The following line explains the comparison with open sacks.

runs.text: ſacos furados por onde paſſa o vento.

lines.note: Wind passes through the perforated sacks. Retain the OCR-supported long-s transcription rather than use semantics to infer s length.
The verb Fuqinagaxi means stretching out by wind. The scan does not support the OCR's space after Fuqin.
Caje fatauo fuqinagaſu describes the wind unfurling flags. Do not supply ga merely from modern grammatical expectations.

runs.text: O vento deſenrola, & estende as bandeiras

lines.note: The Portuguese confirms unfurling and extending flags. The last word is fully visible before the rule; no punctuation is added.
Fuqiſamaxi is cooling by blowing. The long ſ represents s in samashi and must not become f.
Fuqiſucaxi means wind passing through. Typographic s length is retained rather than inferred from meaning.

runs.text: gũa couſa, ou paſſar por antre portas, aruo-

lines.note: The gloss includes passage between doors and trees. Antre is retained as historical Portuguese.
Completes aruores and the list. The short continuation is not to be merged or dropped as blank space.
Fuqit is a clipped final-t form for ill luck, illustrated by fuqitna coto and Yocarazu. A final vowel must not be inserted merely to modernize it.

runs.text: boa, mal eſtreada, ou de ruim ſucceßo.

lines.note: Completes 'not good, badly begun, or of bad outcome'. Succeßo here means outcome, not necessarily success.
Fuqitate is a transitive raising or blowing-up action. Retain the printed tçuru principal part.
Adds raising something by blowing, especially fire below. The paragraph mark divides senses, not physical rows.
Completes raising or waking up the fire. Eſpertar is Portuguese explanatory vocabulary.
Fuqitachi is the intransitive rise of boiling or foam, distinct from the preceding transitive formation.

runs.text: ra, ou eſcumo dalgũa couſa que ſe coze.

lines.note: Describes boiling or foam from something cooking. Retain eſcumo rather than normalize it to familiar espuma.
The scan appears to print Fiqitçume although NINJAL and sense suggest Fuqitçume. Preserve the visible spelling as a possible printing peculiarity; correct clear Portuguese OCR cominu- to continu-.

runs.text: ar algum vento da meſma maneira.

lines.note: Completes continuar, a wind continuing in the same manner. This explains the preceding -tçume compound.
The worn headword is read Fuqitçuqe, uru, eta, with scan and NINJAL support. Final che- and detached gar remain separate; gar occupies the catchword position rather than this row.
